div.head: I Cn 19.2
div.ab: ⁊ æghwylc unriht aweorpe man georne of þysum earde, þæs þe man don mæge,
⁊ æghwylc unriht aworpe man georne of ðisson earde, ðæs ðe man don mæge.
And æghwylc unriht aweorpe mann georne of þissum earde, þæs þe man don mage.
Omnis iniusticia de finibus nostris, quantum possumus, expellatur.
et omnem iniusticiam, in quantum quis poterit, ab hac patria eiciat;
⁊ æghwylc unriht aworpe man georne of ðisson earde, ðæs ðe man don mæge.
And æghwylc unriht aweorpe man georne of þysum earde, þæs þe man don mæge
Und jedes Unrecht entferne man eifrig aus diesem Lande, so weit als man es zu thun vermag;
And let every injustice be eagerly cast out of this country, as far as it can be done;
And every injustice shall be zealously cast out from this land, as far as it is possible to do so.
And all injustice is to be banished from this land as much as possible.

note.seg: Den Gedanken wiederholt II 1. Vgl. Cnuts Lob: leges oppressit iniquas, iustitiam et equitatem extulit im Encom. Emmae (ed. Mon. Germ., SS. XIX 520)
II 1 repeats the thought. Cf. the praise of Cnut: leges oppressit iniquas, iustitiam et equitatem extulit in the Encom. Emmae (ed. Mon. Germ., SS. XIX 520)
